Useful for developers weighing which AI coding tool to adopt.

item.description: A V2EX user documented how to register a .com domain for ₺75 TRY per year (roughly 10 RMB) through the Turkey region of Google Workspace, with no real-name verification or phone number required, and the same route works for .net, .org and .app. Payment is bundled with the Workspace trial subscription and a +86 number can be attached later; the author warns you should transfer the domain out before cancelling the subscription, since the domain becomes inaccessible for login afterward.

item.description: StepFun's terminal arm launched STEPX Neo, its first agent-centric phone, priced at 3999 yuan with first sales on October 16, alongside the Step AOS 1.0 agent-native OS and Step Studio developer tools; buyers also get 100 billion tokens per month for 12 months. Its signature hardware twist is a rear display that shows the agent's states such as waking, listening and thinking, plus a six-microphone array and Whisper 1.0 pickup algorithm for whispered speech in noisy environments.

item.title: [hackernews] Redesigning source control at Anthropic
item.description: Anthropic's post explains why source control became its biggest development bottleneck once daily merges grew more than tenfold, and how the company migrated to an in-house version control system in five months. It's an engineering write-up aimed at developers curious about tooling under AI-heavy coding workflows.

item.title: [hackernews] Containment and monitoring failures are to blame for AI hacking reports: experts
item.description: Cybersecurity experts say the recent alarming hacking reports blamed on AI come down to containment and monitoring failures at AI labs, not agents acting with minds of their own. For CISOs, that reframes the job as vetting AI vendors and tightening security basics rather than treating the models themselves as the threat.

item.title: [hackernews] Ledger confirms spy chip implant behind wallet crypto thefts
item.description: Ledger has confirmed that a spy chip implanted in its hardware was behind cryptocurrency thefts from its wallets. The linked page isn't summarized here; this post is just a set of links to coverage on heise and crypto.news plus research write-ups, so details beyond the title aren't available.

item.title: [hackernews] AI is a tool and using it well takes skill
item.description: This piece responds to Rich Hickey's essay "'AI' is Not a Tool," arguing that automation and tool use can coexist rather than being mutually exclusive. The author's point is that wielding an LLM well is itself a skill, one that depends on feedback loops and judgment instead of simply handing work off to a model.

item.title: [hackernews] Firefox Enterprise
item.description: Firefox Enterprise is Mozilla's enterprise browser offering, designed so organizations can deploy and manage it on their own infrastructure, keeping data, policies and management under their control and auditable. The product page emphasizes data sovereignty, AI governance, and VDI/RBI risk reduction, making it relevant to IT and security teams with compliance requirements.

item.title: [hackernews] Fingerprints are the new cookies
item.description: This demo page fingerprints visitors without cookies: it derives a stable nickname from browser and device traits that survives clearing cookies or connecting through a VPN, and stays consistent in incognito until you switch devices. The author argues ad-funded sites running such scripts could link that identifier to your account data and sell it, undercutting the claim that the data is anonymized.

item.title: [hackernews] 11 year old unsoundness bugs found in Rust borrow checker
item.description: An issue reports unsoundness bugs in Rust's borrow checker that go back about 11 years. In the thread, maintainers add context, noting that Rust's type system is intended to prevent memory unsafety and that they take upholding that promise seriously. That claim is central to Rust's appeal, so anyone writing unsafe code or maintaining the compiler should read it; the note supplied here is all the detail available.

item.description: Developers noticed that Spring AI Alibaba's GitHub Releases page stops at v1.1.2.2, which set off a heated debate in tech groups over whether the project has halted updates and whether Java still has a future in AI applications. The article starts from that observation and digs into the project's release cadence and Java's AI options, for teams weighing a Java-based AI stack.

item.title: [juejin] 每天白嫖 WorkBuddy 100 积分，我让WorkBuddy自己领
item.description: A developer documented how to automate WorkBuddy's daily 100 free credits so the app claims them on its own instead of needing a manual check-in. The author notes they already pay for a membership yet still felt anxious about missing a day, which is what pushed them to automate it. Anyone using WorkBuddy who keeps forgetting the daily claim can follow the same approach.

item.title: [github_trending] debpalash/VoiceStudio
item.description: VoiceStudio, by debpalash, is an open-source, fully local alternative to ElevenLabs. It bundles voice cloning, voice design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription and audiobook creation across 646 languages. Because everything runs locally rather than through a hosted API, it suits developers who care about data privacy or want to avoid commercial subscriptions.

item.title: [github_trending] ifixai-ai/iFixAi
item.description: iFixAi is an open-source tool for independent auditing of AI agents, run either by a human or by the agent itself, to catch mistakes and blind spots before they cause trouble and answer whether an agent is doing what it's supposed to. Its README ships in English, Simplified Chinese, Japanese and Korean, and it has ranked as a Product Hunt daily top post. Aimed at developers who want a reliability check on agent workflows.

item.title: [github_trending] xtool-org/xtool
item.description: xtool-org/xtool is a cross-platform replacement for Xcode: it builds a SwiftPM package into an iOS app, signs and installs it, and talks to Apple Developer Services programmatically from Linux, Windows, WSL or macOS. Aimed at developers who want iOS builds outside a Mac, or in CI, without depending on Xcode itself.

item.title: [github_trending] vxcontrol/pentagi
item.description: PentAGI is a fully autonomous AI agent system built to carry out complex penetration testing tasks; the name stands for Penetration testing Artificial General Intelligence. It maintains a Discord and Telegram community for security researchers and AI enthusiasts, making it relevant to red-teamers and anyone tracking automated security testing.

item.title: [github_trending] NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra
item.description: Ghidra is a software reverse engineering framework built and maintained by the National Security Agency's Research Directorate. It bundles disassembly, decompilation, graphing and scripting for Windows, macOS and Linux binaries across many processor instruction sets, and runs both interactively and in automated mode. Users can extend it with Java or Python, making it a customizable platform for malware analysis and large-team SRE work.

item.title: [github_trending] mksglu/context-mode
item.description: Context Mode is an optimization layer for AI coding agents that sandboxes tool output, which it says cuts context usage by 98%, persists session memory, and enforces routing across 17 platforms via MCP plus hooks. It ships as an npm package under the ELv2 license, aimed at developers whose agents keep blowing through their context window.

item.title: [github_trending] rust-lang/rust
item.description: This is the main source repository for the Rust programming language, holding the compiler, the standard library and the documentation. Rust emphasizes performance and memory efficiency, a fit for critical services, embedded devices and other workloads where speed and a small footprint matter. It is the starting point for learning the language or contributing to the toolchain.

item.title: [github_trending] ntdevlabs/tiny11builder
item.description: Tiny11 Builder is a native WinUI app that turns an official or user-supplied Windows image into a smaller, customized Windows 11 ISO. It offers three build modes, Tiny11 (keeps updates, Defender and recovery), Tiny11 Core (drops servicing and recovery, disables Defender) and Custom (pick components individually), plus a Turbo mode to speed up processing. Core images can't be updated or serviced and protected Custom removals can break Windows, so testing the ISO in a VM first is advised.
